headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no write-conflict pathway is evident, but broad egress from agent A warrants caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing tool with no documented shared channel to Agent B, while Agent B only processes audio/speech files and has no clipboard/MCP/filesystem bridge. A prompt-injection path is therefore not evident in defaults; the remaining risk is limited to unusual manual transfer of text into B.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes Agent A output into Agent B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes from manual to automated.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no shared clipboard.
Treat Agent A output as untrusted text before any reuse.
Disable any future MCP or queue bridge unless provenance checks are added.
Use a human review step before copying text between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B cannot read files or use network egress, and Agent A has broad egress but no documented access to sensitive data classes. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, leakage is not a default pathway; uncertainty remains because Agent A's egress is broad and the pair is unverified.
conditions: IF Agent A is given sensitive text and is allowed to transmit it externally, leakage can occur.
IF a shared workspace is introduced and Agent B gains file read access, audio files could be exposed indirectly.
mitigations: Do not feed secrets or regulated data into Agent A.
Keep Agent B file access disabled unless needed.
Route any sensitive transcription through a local-only path.
Review outbound destinations for Agent A before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has broad network egress but no write or git capabilities are documented, while Agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF Agent A is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as another agent, conflict risk appears.
IF Agent B is reconfigured with write or git permissions, overlapping mutation becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Agent B read-only as documented.
Avoid granting Agent A filesystem or git write permissions in shared locations.
Use separate workspaces for any future writable agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate content that Agent B might consume, but B is an audio-speech model with no action-taking authority, and no evidence shows B automatically treats A's output as authoritative. The cascade is therefore limited to manual or orchestrated reuse of text, not a default autonomous failure mode.
conditions: IF Agent A output is fed into Agent B as ground truth without review, downstream transcription or summarization errors can propagate.
IF a separate orchestrator uses B's output to trigger actions, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between A and B outputs.
Label Agent A output as draft or untrusted.
Do not connect B to any action-taking automation.
Spot-check a sample of A-to-B handoffs for factual drift.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with Agent B touching audio/speech and Agent A having broad egress but no declared regulated-data handling. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to future deployment choices rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF regulated audio or speech data is routed through Agent A's outbound network path, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires residency controls that are not enforced for either agent, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Agent A.
Document data residency for any audio pipeline using Agent B.
Add retention limits before storing transcripts or audio.
Review vendor and hosting terms before production use.
